newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission vague about BA/AA conditions.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission vague about BA/AA conditions.

text.p: The European Commission declined on Monday to confirm press reports that it had asked British Airways and American Airlines to cede 350 weekly slots at Heathrow Airport to win European Union approval for their alliance.
But a Commission source, referring to an article in the Financial Times, said "It's not a million miles from the truth."
The Commission's position at this stage was a "maximalist one", designed to secure the best concessions to safeguard competition on the U.S.-British air route, the source said.

Sarah Lambert, spokeswoman for Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock, restated the Commission's position that the deal cannot go through as it currently stands. "We are in the process of looking at possible remedies," she told reporters.

The Commission is not expected to give its final decision on the alliance before October. Britain's Office of Fair Trading proposed last year that it be cleared on the condition that the airlines give up 168 weekly landing and takeoff slots at London's congested Heathrow Airport.
But EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has said that is not enough. U.S. airlines have requested more than 300 slots.
